note: Common Control Framework. A safeguard is the operated object: it carries one evidence requirement and one evaluation rule, and satisfies many framework requirements. Framework readiness is derived from safeguard posture, not the other way round. Every control_id under `satisfies` must exist in controls/catalog.json. A mapping is `reviewed` once a human has confirmed the requirements are genuinely the same obligation; `proposed` mappings were matched by title theme and are reported separately so unconfirmed work is never counted as attested coverage.

safeguards.objective: Evaluate AI systems regularly for safety, fairness and bias, and explainability against the risks identified for their context, and track the risks that current metrics cannot measure.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence of the latest safety evaluation, including fail-safe behaviour beyond knowledge limits; fairness and bias results with the populations tested; model explanation and output-interpretation documentation; and a tracking record for trustworthiness risks that current metrics cannot measure. An overdue evaluation or an unresolved result above risk tolerance is an open violation.

safeguards.title: AI incident handling and reporting
safeguards.objective: Identify, triage, respond to and recover from AI incidents and previously unknown AI risks, and communicate them to affected AI actors, providers and authorities where required.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: `siem-alerts` detections and `ticketing` incident records classify AI incidents, such as harmful output, model misuse, data leakage through an AI system or a safety failure, with owner, severity and timeline. safeguards.title: Third-party model and dataset provenance (AI-BOM)
safeguards.objective: Record the origin, version, license and supplier of every third-party model, dataset and AI component in an AI bill of materials, monitor the pre-trained models in use, and keep contingency plans for failures in high-risk third-party AI.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence: a current AI bill of materials (CycloneDX or SPDX, importable through the AIBOM store) lists each pre-trained model, dataset and AI service with source, version, license, supplier and responsible party. `kubernetes-cluster` image provenance covers the serving container images, not model weights. A production model missing from the AI-BOM, or a high-risk third-party AI dependency without a contingency plan, is an open violation.

safeguards.title: Human oversight of AI systems
safeguards.objective: Define, staff and exercise human oversight for each AI system, with documented knowledge limits and trained operators who can intervene in, override or stop its outputs.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: `runtime-gateway` policy decisions show human-approval and intervention steps on agent tool calls. Attested evidence documents the oversight design per AI system, its knowledge limits and output-use guidance, and operator competence records. A high-risk AI system without an assigned, trained overseer is an open violation.

safeguards.title: AI training and evaluation data governance
safeguards.objective: Govern the data used to train, fine-tune and evaluate AI systems: its lineage, quality, representativeness and preparation, and the lawful basis or consent for any personal data in it.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence per dataset: source and lineage, collection and preparation steps, quality and representativeness checks including bias examination, personal-data content with its lawful basis or consent, human-subject protections for evaluation data drawn from people, and approval for use. A dataset in use without a lineage record, or personal data without a documented lawful basis, is an open violation.

safeguards.title: AI transparency and user disclosure
safeguards.objective: Tell users and deployers that they are dealing with an AI system, what it is for, its capabilities and limits, and where to get more information, and examine the accountability risks of what is disclosed.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence of the user-facing AI disclosures and instructions for use per AI system (purpose, capabilities, limitations, human-oversight measures, contact point), the technical documentation provided to each audience, and a review of transparency and accountability risks. An AI system that interacts with people without a current disclosure is an open violation.

safeguards.title: Access control for AI inference endpoints and agent tools
safeguards.objective: Authenticate callers of AI inference endpoints and authorize each agent tool call against a least-privilege policy at runtime, recording every decision.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: `runtime-gateway` tool-call, policy-decision and runtime-block events show each agent tool call and inference request evaluated against policy with the caller identity and the decision recorded. A tool call allowed in breach of policy, or an unauthenticated inference endpoint, is an open violation.

safeguards.title: AI model change, rollback and decommissioning
safeguards.objective: Control AI model and system updates, keep the ability to supersede, disengage or roll back a system performing outside its intended use, and retire AI systems without increasing risk.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: `ticketing` change records and Attested evidence per AI system version: approved updates with the measured improvement, a tested rollback or disengagement path with a named owner, and decommissioning records covering model, data and endpoint retirement. A production AI system without a tested disengagement path is an open violation.

safeguards.objective: Assess the benefits and costs of each AI system and the likelihood and magnitude of its impacts on individuals, groups and society, including viable non-AI alternatives, before and during use.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence of a current impact assessment per AI system recording expected benefits, potential costs of errors, the likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact drawn from past incidents and external feedback, the non-AI alternatives considered, and the resources required to manage the risks. An AI system in production without a current assessment is an open violation.
